Here is the `/luz` help. It writes nothing.

| Chat | What it does | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/luz` | Starts a site. It asks questions, shows a plan, waits for "go", writes the starter page, then finishes it with you. | Yes, after "go" |
| `/luz new <landing, blog, app or docs>` | Does the same without asking the kind of site. | Yes, after "go" |
| `/luz doctor` | Shows the project, its assistants, and the skills and agents it has. | No |
| `/luz check [path]` | Checks the front matter of the project's skills and agents, or of the path you give. | No |
| `/luz facts` | Shows the versions, kinds of site and stacks of this release. | No |
| `/luz agents` | Lists the luz-ai agents. | No |
| `/luz add <name>` | Adds the agent with that name, after asking for its fields. | Yes, after "go" |
| `/luz help` | Shows this table. | No |

The script's own `--help` lists these commands:
- `init`: installs the skill for an assistant. Run it in a terminal with `npx @luz-ds/ai init --target <assistant>`. It isn't a `/luz` subcommand.
- `site new`: writes the starter page. `--dry-run` shows what it would write first.
- `agent`: lists agents or adds one.
- `facts`, `doctor` and `check`: read-only.

Add `--json` to get one JSON object. Exit code 0 means nothing blocks, 1 means a problem blocks, and 2 means the command was used wrongly.

To start a site, run `/luz` or tell me what you want, for example "make me a landing page with LUZ".
